title: Past tenses, present perfect and going to
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: Past simple: statements, negatives and questions
lessons.explanation: Use the past simple for finished actions. Regular verbs add -ed (visited); irregular verbs have special forms (bought, wrote, saw). For negatives use didn't (did not) plus the base verb: She didn't go to school. For questions use did plus the subject and the base verb: Did you see the film? After did and didn't the main verb has no past ending: not She didn't went.

examples.en: I visited my aunt last week.
She didn't go to school.
Did you see the film?

pt.explanation: Use o passado simples para ações concluídas. Verbos regulares recebem -ed (visited); verbos irregulares têm formas próprias (bought, wrote, saw). lessons.title: Past continuous for ongoing and interrupted events
lessons.explanation: Use was or were plus the -ing form for an action that was in progress at a past moment: They were playing football. Use was with I, he, she and it and were with you, we and they. The past continuous often describes a longer action interrupted by a shorter one in the past simple, joined by when: I was cooking when the phone rang.

examples.en: I was cooking when the phone rang.
They were playing football.
What were you doing at eight o'clock?

pt.title: Passado contínuo para ações em andamento e interrompidas
pt.explanation: Use was ou were mais a forma do verbo terminada em -ing para uma ação que estava acontecendo em determinado momento do passado: They were playing football. Use was com I, he, she e it; use were com you, we e they. O passado contínuo costuma descrever uma ação mais longa que foi interrompida por outra, mais curta, no passado simples; elas podem ser ligadas por when: I was cooking when the phone rang.

examples.en: I was cooking when the phone rang.
examples.pt: Eu estava cozinhando quando o telefone tocou.

examples.en: They were playing football.
What were you doing at eight o'clock?
examples.pt: O que você estava fazendo às oito?

lessons.title: Present perfect for experience and recent events
lessons.explanation: Form the present perfect with have or has plus the past participle: I have visited Paris. She has just finished. Use it for life experience and for recent events without a finished time. Frequent markers: ever (in questions), never, just, already, yet. Past participles: regular verbs add -ed; irregular ones must be learned (eaten, seen, been, gone). Do not use it with a finished time like yesterday.

examples.en: I have visited Paris.
She has just finished.
Have you ever eaten sushi?

lessons.title: Going to for plans and predictions
lessons.explanation: Use am, is or are plus going to and the base verb for plans and intentions: I am going to visit my aunt. Use it also for predictions based on what you can see now: Look at the clouds. It is going to rain. Questions put be first: What are you going to do? Do not drop be and do not add -s or -ing to the main verb.

Look at the clouds. It is going to rain.
What are you going to do?
